title: Senegal become first side to book Afcon 2027 spot

Senegal became the first side to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) before Egypt and Ivory Coast were among five sides who missed out on the chance to join them.

Led by new head coach Patrick Vieira, Senegal had moved to the brink of a place at the finals by beating Sudan 4-2 on Monday, and the Teranga Lions had their ticket confirmed with two games to spare in Group J when Mozambique secured a 1-0 victory away against Ethiopia.
Algeria, DR Congo, Egypt and the Ivorians could have progressed with away wins, but all four sides failed to pick up three points.

Brighton forward Yankuba Minteh was on target as The Gambia came from behind to lead Ivory Coast 2-1 in Group C, but Christ Inao Oulai grabbed a stoppage-time equaliser after Scorpions striker Muhammed Badamosi was sent off in the 90th minute.
Egypt were held to a goalless draw in Malawi, Sierra Leone claimed a late point against the Congolese and Algeria suffered a 3-0 defeat in Togo.
Angola beat South Sudan 1-0 in Juba and would have qualified had Egypt claimed all three points in the other match in Group B.

Published30 OctoberFive more sides, including Morocco and Cameroon, could join Senegal in booking a spot at next year's finals in East Africa as the fourth round of fixtures culminates on Tuesday.
Meanwhile, Nigeria are in danger of missing out on Afcon for the first time since 2017 after the Super Eagles failed to beat tournament co-hosts Tanzania.
Tunisia, who have appeared at a record 17 consecutive editions of the tournament, could also be absent after their winless start in Group H was extended with a 1-1 draw in Libya.
The final two rounds of qualifiers will be held in March next year, with Afcon 2027 scheduled to be held in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda from 19 June to 17 July.
Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Malawi goalkeeper George Chikooka helped deny Mohamed Salah's Egypt an early passage to the Afcon 2027 finals in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda
Seven-time Afcon winners Egypt knew victory in Lilongwe could take them to the finals but were frustrated by an inspired second-half showing from Malawi goalkeeper George Chikooka.

After Pharaohs captain Mohamed Salah had hit the outside of the post from a tight angle, Chikooka denied Trezeguet and Haissem Hassan before also making fine stops from Mohamed Hany and Ibrahim Adel in stoppage time.
Egypt move on to eight points in Group B, two points behind Angola after Miro's first-half effort secured a 1-0 victory for the Palancas Negras in Juba.
There was drama as Ivory Coast salvaged a draw in Bakau through Inao Oulai's 98th-minute goal, which denied The Gambia a third win in Group C.
The Ivorians lead the pool on 10 points, with The Gambia on seven and Ghana on six following the Black Stars' back-to-back wins over Somalia.

DR Congo appeared on track to progress from Group E as Junior Kadile gave the Leopards a half-time lead in their away tie against Sierra Leone, but Alie Conteh netted in the 94th minute for the West Africans.
